meta.title: Notebooks: Git-Backed Re-Clones, Un-Versioned Migrates Debt

views.label: Two very different starting points
views.note: Git-backed code lives in Git, not the workspace. Un-versioned code is technical debt about to become permanent.

views.label: Audit regardless of path
views.note: Cloud storage paths, catalog names, and DBFS mounts get hardcoded into notebook code no matter how it was exported.

views.label: Migration is the natural point to fix this
views.note: Carrying un-versioned notebooks into the target workspace just relocates the same problem, permanently.

cards.title: Git-backed is usually the simplest part
items: The code and history live in Git, not the workspace — re-clone the same remote into target
Re-establish Git credentials for the target workspace against the provider
If CI/CD deploys from the repo, confirm the deployment target mapping points at target, not source

cards.title: Un-versioned notebooks are debt about to become permanent
items: No Git repo means no change history and no code review trail
Carrying it forward unchanged just relocates the same problem into the new workspace
Migration is the natural point to move it into a repo — export/import is the fallback, not the goal

cards.title: Audit runs regardless of which path got you here
items: Cloud storage paths (abfss://, s3://, gs://) need the cloud-mapping path-rewrite applied
Catalog/schema names and any hardcoded cluster/warehouse IDs need target values
DBFS mount paths migrate to Unity Catalog volumes or external locations, never recreated as mounts
